description:
You are a medical scientist performing 3D volumetric analysis of a human brain MRI scan. A 16-bit grayscale MRI image stack (27 axial slices) is available at ~/Fiji_Data/raw/mri/mri_stack.tif. Voxel dimensions are documented in ~/Fiji_Data/raw/mri/voxel_info.txt.

Your goal: Perform 3D segmentation and volumetric measurement of two distinct brain regions:

(1) BRIGHT REGION: Segment the bright brain tissue (excluding skull and background). Apply a threshold to isolate tissue signal, then use 3D connected components to identify the main brain mass. Measure its volume in mm3.

(2) VENTRICLES: Within the brain mass, identify the dark CSF-filled ventricles (hypo-intense regions). Apply an inverse threshold within the brain mask to isolate ventricle-like structures. Measure total ventricle volume in mm3.

For each structure, compute: volume_voxels, volume_mm3, and (if possible) surface area and sphericity.

Save results to ~/Fiji_Data/results/volumetry/volume_measurements.csv with columns: structure_name,volume_voxels,volume_mm3,surface_area_mm2,sphericity. Save orthogonal views (XY, XZ, YZ projections) to ~/Fiji_Data/results/volumetry/orthogonal_views.tif. Save a text report to ~/Fiji_Data/results/volumetry/volumetry_report.txt summarizing both measurements and noting whether ventricle volume is < 5% of brain volume (typical in healthy brain).

metadata.dataset: ImageJ MRI Stack - human brain axial MRI
